text: Four letters show up constantly in ServiceNow careers: CSA, CAD, CIS, and CTA. Across courses one through thirteen of this path, you built real skills that map directly onto these credentials. This lesson lays out, precisely, what each one certifies and how they actually relate to each other — because the relationship is not a simple straight line, and getting it wrong leads to wasted study time.

CSA, Certified System Administrator, is the foundational credential: baseline competence across the platform itself, built in this path's Platform Fundamentals and System Administration courses. Every CIS specialization lists CSA as a formal prerequisite, and that reflects a real dependency, not a technicality — you can't implement a module's workflows without already understanding tables, roles, and configuration at the CSA level. So CSA goes first, regardless of which direction you head afterward. It's the floor the rest of the ladder stands on.

CAD, Certified Application Developer, certifies building custom applications — scripting, Flow Designer, application scoping — the territory of courses four through seven. CIS, Certified Implementation Specialist, is not one credential but a family of them, each tied to a specific module: CIS-ITSM, CIS-CSM, CIS-HR, CIS-Discovery. And CTA, Certified Technical Architect, certifies architecting an entire program, not just one module.

Past CSA, the ladder forks based on the kind of work you want, not which credential is supposedly better. Building new functionality points toward CAD. Implementing a specific module for a real business points toward a CIS specialization. Plenty of working consultants eventually hold both — but as a sequencing matter, pick the branch that matches the depth you actually built in courses one through thirteen. And here's the part most new ServiceNow professionals get wrong: CTA is not simply the next certification after CAD or CIS. It's gated behind real, demonstrated implementation experience across multiple real projects — the kind this course's own capstone has you start practicing.

CSA is the floor, CAD and CIS are the branches matched to the work you want, and CTA sits apart, earned through years of real experience rather than another exam. Next up: choosing a specific CIS specialization, grounded in what you actually built hands-on depth in across this path's thirteen courses.
